title: PRD: Progressive-envelope output contract, resumable tool-handoff, and error taxonomy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a deterministic, incremental output envelope and tool-invocation contract that supports streaming partial JSON, clear error classes, idempotent tool handoffs, and resumability checkpoints. This PRD clarifies behavior required from model-serving and SDKs, acceptance criteria for QA, and rollout constraints for Redwood Hosted and Dedicated customers. The contract must preserve developer ergonomics (parseable fragments), enable low-latency streaming, and allow automatic safe fallback to a non-streaming envelope when incompatibilities are detected.
scope: Define envelope framing, sequence numbering, compact checkpoint markers, error taxonomy (transient/retryable, repairable, fatal), tool call handshake (idempotency token, function signature validation), SDK parsing expectations, server-side telemetry hooks, and end-to-end test cases. Deliverables: formal spec, SDK tests, runtime feature flags and canary plan, and a QA test harness that simulates partial emissions and mid-stream failures.
out_of_scope: Changes to model training or prompt formats beyond emission framing. Deep changes to existing log storage retention. Third-party tool runtimes (customer managed) that cannot be proxied by Redwood Private without additional integration work.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope framing: every streamed emission must start with a single top-level envelope header JSON object ("env") containing a stable request_id, proto_version="v2", and sequence_number=1 for the first fragment.

Incremental fragments: each fragment must be a self-describing object with keys: sequence_number (int), partial_payload (string) which is either valid JSON when combined with previous fragments OR an explicit continuation marker. SDKs must be able to reassemble fragments deterministically.

Checkpoint markers: server emits checkpoint tokens every N fragments (configurable; default 8). Checkpoint includes stable resume_token and last_applied_sequence. Resume_token must be usable by the server to rehydrate KV cache and resume at next sequence_number without double-invoking tool calls.

Tool-handshake: for any function/tool invocation the model must emit a tool_invoke envelope that includes function_name, args_schema_hash, idempotency_token, and expected_response_deadline_ms. The runtime must validate args_schema_hash against the function registry and reject mismatches with a repairable error code (see errors).

Idempotency semantics: if a resume occurs and the runtime observes a tool_invoke with an idempotency_token previously applied, the runtime must not re-run the tool; it must return the cached tool result or a stable error if the original result is unavailable.

Error taxonomy: errors are classified as transient/retryable, repairable (schema mismatch or missing data), and fatal. Each error emission must include error_class, error_code (short string), human_message, and optional recovery_suggestion. SDKs must surface recovery_suggestion to developers.

Partial-parse safety: any prefix of the stream that ends at a fragment boundary must be parseable by the SDK into an object indicating completeness=false. Parsers must never throw on valid fragment boundaries.

Fallback behavior: when the client explicitly opts into strict mode, any repairable error must trigger an immediate non-streaming reissue of the request (server-side) rather than best-effort repairs. In permissive mode, the runtime may attempt to auto-repair within configured thresholds.

Observability: every request must emit telemetry with request_id, model_version, route, latency_p50/95/99, fragment_count, checkpoint_count, tool_invocation_count, error_rate, and resume_attempts. These fields must be queryable in Console dashboards by release rollout.

Testing: unit tests for envelope framing, resume_token roundtrip, and idempotent tool behavior; integration tests that simulate network drop at fragment boundaries and verify resume semantics; chaos tests where the tool returns inconsistent results and runtime must detect divergence and surface a repairable error.

Backward compatibility: when client presents Accept-Envelope: v1 header, server must fall back to previous non-resumable streaming contract and log a compatibility warning. New v2 behavior must be opt-in for Dedicated customers during canary.

Canary rollout constraints: feature flagged; initial canary limited to 2% of hosted traffic and a single Dedicated customer environment. Blocker conditions to halt rollout: >0.5% increase in total token latency P95, >0.2% increase in fatal error rate, or any production data leak incident tied to resume_token misuse.

Docs and SDKs: release notes, a concise QuickStart for v2 envelopes, and parsers in Node/Python/Go must be available at launch. SDKs must provide helper to automatically perform resume using stored resume_token.
Security: resume_token must be opaque and short-lived (TTL <= 24h) and must not contain unencrypted customer data. KMS policy review required before GA (see security_review_required=true).
success_metrics: Streaming parse success rate >= 99.9% in canary
Resumption correctness: on simulated network drops, 100% of resumed sessions must complete without duplicate tool execution
No increase in fatal error rate above baseline during canary
Observed developer reported parsing bugs <= 2 in first 30 days after GA
test_plan: Unit: envelope encode/decode roundtrip tests for fragments and checkpoints
Integration: server + SDK resume flow with recorded tool responses to assert idempotency
Load: simulate 5000 concurrent streaming sessions with mid-stream disconnects to validate checkpointing and resume throughput
Chaos: arbitrary reordering and duplicate fragments injected by a network proxy to verify parser robustness
Security: token fuzzing and TTL expiry verification, confirm no sensitive payloads in resume_token
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated in runtime and SDK. 2) Internal dogfood on staging for 1 week with automated tests. 3) Hosted canary at 2% traffic for 3 days; observe telemetry and SLA metrics. 4) Invite one Dedicated customer to early access for 7 days. 5) Gradual ramp every 24h (+10% traffic) if metrics within thresholds. 6) GA and SDK stable release when canary OK.
